ev.q: CDC was notified of 119 B. stabilis patient infections among 10 states meeting the case definition
Among 102 patients with vital status information, 14 (14%) deaths were reported
Among 117 patients with available information, 104 (89%) are known to have undergone ultrasonography during their admission
Median interval from hospital admission to detection of B. stabilis infection was 1 day (range = 0–118 days).

public_health_question.v: What was the source and extent of a multistate outbreak of Burkholderia stabilis infections linked to contaminated nonsterile ultrasound gel?

ev.q: In 2021, a total of 119 BCC infections were associated with multiple lots of nonsterile ultrasound gel contaminated with BCC organisms.
Outbreak of Burkholderia stabilis Infections Associated with Contaminated Nonsterile, Multiuse Ultrasound Gel
Outbreak of Burkholderia stabilis Infections Associated with Contaminated Nonsterile, Multiuse Ultrasound Gel — 10 States, May–September 2021
with the assistance of state and local health departments, which collected this information from health care facilities.
identified 119 B. stabilis infections in 10 U.S. states, leading to the national recall

equity.level_reason: Only age and sex appear, as descriptive characteristics of cases in the table; no social-position framing.

ev.q: The median patient age was 61 years (range = 4 days–92 years).

notes: Descriptive case series within an outbreak investigation; no group comparisons or exposed vs unexposed analysis, so data_focus is limited. WGS/rep-PCR relatedness defines case status and is not a procedure. FDA lot testing (8 of 13 lots contaminated) is product investigation, not a patient outcome analysis.
view_issues: Text gives 103 (94%) of 117 with ultrasound-guided procedures, but the table denominator is 109. Text says Eco-Gel 200 used in 31 (26%) of all infections; the table gives 31 (79) of 39 as 'Eco-Med 200'. Table age median n = 68.
